messages:
katie (PM): quick review please for the "latency snapshot" card mock. idea: compact row that can expand into a panel. key: p95 visibility, quick throughput, and an unobtrusive sampling control. mock: https://figma.redwood/latency-snapshot

jake (Design): I tried two directions: 1) single compact line with hover details; 2) small-multiple mini-charts per model inline. small-multiples help product teams compare quickly but are tight on mobile.

maria (Product): small-multiples are compelling for model comparisons. can we collapse to single row on phones? priority: ensure p95 is readable at glance.

sam (Eng-Frontend): implementation note: single-line spark + microbars for throughput is easiest. small-multiples require separate queries per card unless we aggregate server-side. can add server aggregation endpoint but takes time. also recommend lazy-load the heat stripe (tiny vertical heatmap) only on expand.

li (Eng-ML): backend can provide an aggregated small-multiple payload: one call that returns p50/p95/p99 arrays per model. will add headers: `X-Sample-Window` and `X-Sample-Confidence` to describe sampling scope. Also can include `sample_signal: uniform|prefix|adaptive`.

anya (A11y): accessibility checklist: visible focus for expand toggle, ensure chart data is exposed via an accessible table button "Open data table", color-blind friendly palette for heat stripe, and ensure all controls are keyboard operable. Also avoid using color alone to indicate severity.

jake (Design): proposed copy for sampling toggle: label "Sampling" with options: Auto, Full, 10%, 1%, Custom. Tooltip text: "Adjust how many requests are shown; lower sampling reduces cost but may miss rare spikes." shorter on mobile.

maria (Product): prefer copy: "Sampling — Auto (est. 12%)" as default in expanded view but on compact card show only an icon with tooltip. keeps compactness.

sam (Eng-Frontend): icon-only on compact is good. avoid long badges. add an inline helper pin when sample estimate is low: "Sample low — p99 not reliable". that should be a subtle text, not an alert.

li (Eng-ML): our estimate will include a confidence band: e.g., "12% (±4%)". we can flag `low_confidence: true` if sample_count < 200. frontend can decide to hide p99 in that case.

anya (A11y): if p99 hidden, expose that via aria-live: "P99 hidden due to low sample size" so screen reader users aren't confused when a metric disappears. Also ensure tooltip content is reachable via keyboard and described with aria-describedby.

jake (Design): UX layout idea: compact card shows left: spark (p50/p95), middle: throughput mini-bar, right: icon for sampling + expand chevron. expand opens a panel with large p95 chart, heat stripe, timepicker, and a dropdown for sampling. Panel should have a clear close button and ESC binding.

sam (Eng-Frontend): performance: use canvas for the heat stripe and fallback SVG for a11y. we'll memoize series and keep re-renders minimal. also throttle hover tooltips to prevent jank when scrubbing.

maria (Product): analytics: track expand_clicks, sampling_changes, and heatmap_open. KPI: reduce mean time to detect latency regressions by 20% in the canary group.

katie (PM): rollout: feature flag `latency_snapshot_v1`, enable for internal teams then ~10% of orgs. li/sam please add API and endpoint, jake/anya finalize assets.

ui-bot: preview deployed at https://staging.redwood/preview/latency-snapshot/1765449999 5; feature flag=latency_snapshot_v1

li (Eng-ML): last note: return `sample_window_ms` and `sample_count` so UI can compute whether p99 is reliable. will get this into the dev API by EOD Friday.

jake (Design): thanks. action items: I'll update figma with compact/mobile collapse and new sampling icon; anya please draft microcopy for a11y messages; sam to stub frontend routes. will follow up with updated link.
